solutions.check: grid rebuilt from the blog's light list (unique); every answer written into it with each crossing agreeing

clue.text: Acts badly after work at keyboard getting the same parts?

indicators.note: the rearranged letters come after the keyboard word in the answer

parts.note: to type is to work at a keyboard

indicators.note: the word acts is done badly, so its letters are put in a poor new order

explanation.surface: An actor who performs poorly after a spell of typing keeps landing identical roles.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Acts' looks like the verb of the surface, but 'badly' scrambles it; 'after' sets the scrambled word behind the keyboard work. 'parts' are acting roles, not components.
explanation.definitionFit: An actor who is typecast is repeatedly given roles of one kind, hence the question mark.

clue.text: He could be tough, lacking love?

definitions.text: He could be tough, lacking love?

indicators.note: the letters of the word tough could be rearranged into something else
lacking says a letter is left out of the rearranged pool

parts.note: love is zero in tennis, the letter O

explanation.surface: A musing on whether a hard man might be tough but unloving.
explanation.walkthrough: Rearrange TOUGH without its O ('lacking love'); the whole clue also describes the answer, a tough man short on tenderness.
explanation.definitionFit: A violent ruffian is a hard, rough man who shows no kindness, as the whole clue suggests.

clue.text: Shellfish that's uncooked put into empty pan

indicators.note: put into says one piece goes inside another
an empty pan has lost its inside letter, leaving only its outer pair

parts.note: uncooked food is raw

explanation.surface: Raw seafood placed into a cooking pan with nothing else in it.
explanation.walkthrough: 'empty' means a word with its middle removed, here the A of pan; 'put into' then fills the gap.
explanation.definitionFit: This small decapod crustacean is a common edible shellfish.

clue.text: Sweet having me in calmer race, somehow

indicators.note: somehow says the letters end up arranged in some other way

explanation.surface: A dessert found in the middle of a quieter sort of race.
explanation.definitionFit: This set custard with caramel sauce is a dessert, and a sweet is British for a dessert course.

clue.text: Unruffled sound from cow in south

indicators.note: in places the cow's noise inside the abbreviation

parts.note: Sth is a written abbreviation for south
a cow says moo

explanation.surface: A calm moo heard from a cow somewhere in the south.
explanation.walkthrough: 'in' puts MOO inside STH, an abbreviation of south.
explanation.definitionFit: Something unruffled is even and calm, without bumps or agitation.

clue.text: Produced money, we hear

indicators.note: we hear says the word is taken by its pronunciation

parts.note: bread is slang for money

explanation.surface: Someone generating cash, so the rumour goes.
explanation.walkthrough: BREAD (slang for money) is pronounced the same as the answer.
explanation.definitionFit: Bred, as in raised offspring or livestock, is a past-tense synonym of produced.

clue.text: Having climbed moor? That is right, it's more spacious

indicators.note: in a down entry climbing means reading upwards, so the moor word goes backwards

parts.note: i.e. is Latin id est, that is

explanation.surface: A hiker, having scaled a moor, finds it roomy up there.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Having climbed' only signals a reversal because this is a down entry, read bottom to top; 'it's' is a link before the definition.
explanation.definitionFit: Comparative of roomy: having more room, so larger inside.

clue.text: Tipping hat, one overseeing man, hard-working

indicators.note: in a down entry, overseeing means standing above the next piece
tipping the hat tips the word over, reading it backwards

parts.note: a lid is slang for a hat
one is the Roman numeral I
a gent is a man

explanation.surface: A man tips his hat to a diligent supervisor.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Tipping' turns LID into DIL; 'overseeing' puts DIL and I above GENT in the down entry.
explanation.definitionFit: A synonym: someone hard-working is industrious and careful in their efforts.

clue.text: Nasty stain mars a chair arm initially — protective cloth found

indicators.note: a nasty stain mangles the letters into a fresh arrangement
initially takes the opening letter of each of the two words

explanation.surface: A dirty stain spoils a chair arm, and a protective cover turns up.
explanation.walkthrough: 'initially' gives CA from chair arm; 'Nasty' rearranges these with STAIN MARS A.
explanation.definitionFit: Example: a small cloth laid over a chair back or arm to keep hair oil off the upholstery.

clue.text: Custom from American era

parts.note: US is short for United States, so it stands for American
an age is an era

explanation.surface: A tradition handed down from an American period of history.
explanation.definitionFit: A synonym: established usage is habitual practice or custom.

clue.text: Personal target leading to footballer's error

parts.note: own means personal, belonging to oneself
a goal is a target

explanation.surface: Aiming at one's own target ends in a soccer player's blunder.
explanation.definitionFit: A football mistake of scoring into your side's net, crediting the opponents.

clue.text: Coming in holding that isn't regularly amusing

indicators.note: holding means one word keeps the other inside it

parts.note: entering means coming in

indicators.note: regularly takes every other letter of the words that isn't

explanation.surface: Something arriving with a holding that is, at intervals, not amusing.
explanation.walkthrough: 'regularly' picks the odd letters of that isn't, ignoring the apostrophe; 'holding' splits the synonym for coming in after its fifth letter.
explanation.definitionFit: A synonym: something entertaining diverts and delights its audience.

clue.text: MP should get back in here

definitions.text: MP should get back in here

parts.words: MP should get back in here
parts.note: a constituency where a sitting Member of Parliament is sure to be re-elected

explanation.surface: A constituency so reliable its member is bound to return to parliament.
explanation.walkthrough: 'get back in' reads as returning somewhere, but means being re-elected.
explanation.definitionFit: A constituency with a large, dependable majority, so its MP will be voted in again.

clue.text: TV feature perhaps recalled in tuneful air, eastern

indicators.note: recalled says the hidden letters are read backwards
the clue word that says the letters sit inside the next words

parts.note: the letters run across the end of one word into the next

explanation.surface: A melodious eastern tune remembered from a television programme.
explanation.walkthrough: The letters LAIREA sit in tuneful air, eastern; 'recalled' turns them round.
explanation.definitionFit: Example: a rooftop antenna is a feature of a television set-up, picking up the broadcast signal.

clue.text: One working no longer referring to Scottish island

parts.note: re means about or referring to
Tiree is an island in the Inner Hebrides of Scotland

explanation.surface: A former worker discussing a Scottish island, perhaps where they settled.
explanation.walkthrough: Tiree is a small island off the west coast of Scotland.
explanation.definitionFit: A pensioner who has stopped employment is someone who no longer works.

clue.text: Warn about edges of route in overcrowded area

indicators.note: about means the word warn goes around the other letters
edges of takes the first and last letters of the word route

explanation.surface: A warning about the margins of a road through a crowded district.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Warn' looks like the clue's verb but is taken literally as letters; 'about' wraps it round the piece from 'edges of'.
explanation.definitionFit: Figurative sense: a maze of cramped streets or buildings, like rabbits' burrows.

clue.text: Disconcert painter, non-drinker, extremely likable

parts.note: RA is a Royal Academician, a painter
TT is teetotal, someone who does not drink

indicators.note: extremely means take the extreme letters of likable

explanation.surface: Unsettling an artist who abstains from alcohol and is very pleasant.
explanation.walkthrough: 'extremely' gives LE, the end letters of likable.
explanation.definitionFit: A synonym: to unnerve or fluster someone is to make them lose composure.

clue.text: Unexpectedly gave a car next, spending too much

indicators.note: unexpectedly says the letters come out in a surprising new order

explanation.surface: Someone surprisingly gave away another car, a lavish overspend.
explanation.definitionFit: A noun phrase fit: lavish, wasteful outlay of money is excess.

clue.text: Pursue ornament with engraving

definitions.meaning: to go after or hunt something
to decorate metal by engraving or embossing it

explanation.definitionFit: A double meaning: go after something, or decorate metal by tooling patterns into it.

clue.text: Care for those experiencing niggling delays at first

indicators.note: at first takes the opening letter of each word

explanation.surface: Looking after people suffering irritating hold-ups.
explanation.definitionFit: A synonym: to look after a patient or a garden is to attend to it.

clue.text: Advance payment showing sincerity

definitions.meaning: a deposit paid as a pledge to seal a bargain

explanation.definitionFit: Double meaning: a deposit sealing a deal, or describing someone serious and wholehearted.

clue.text: Introduction of secure, healthy, source of gas

indicators.note: the introduction of a word is its opening letter

parts.note: hale means healthy, as in hale and hearty

explanation.surface: Bringing in a secure, robust supply of fuel.
explanation.definitionFit: Example: this sedimentary rock is fracked for natural gas, so it is a source.

clue.text: Guy from Egypt he obliges

indicators.note: from says the letters are taken out of the words that follow

explanation.surface: A man from Egypt who is happy to help.
explanation.walkthrough: The letters run across Egypt he obliges; 'Guy' is a man's name, not a verb.
explanation.definitionFit: A male first name, so an example of a guy, a man.

clue.text: Find beer possibly as favour

indicators.note: possibly says the letters might be arranged differently

explanation.surface: Locating some beer, perhaps as a good turn.
explanation.walkthrough: 'possibly' rearranges FIND BEER; 'as' is a link.
explanation.definitionFit: A verb sense: to favour someone is to support or side with them, as a friend would.
